text:
incident-bot: Pager: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/generate for customers in us-west-2. p95=2.1s p99=5.6s, streaming stalls observed, error rate up 0.8%. Possible GPU node degradation. Paging on-call (Daniel K).
Daniel K: On it, I'm on-call. Pulling dashboards now. Any noisy deploys?

Alex S: No recent prod deploys in the last 30m. I see a cluster-level spike starting 1800123300 (about 6m ago). Affects two GPU pods on node gpu-node-37 and gpu-node-39.

Priya R: Checking infra alerts: node-exporter shows thermal_throttle events on gpu-node-37 and ECC error counts increasing on gpu1. Query: `sum(rate(nvidia_ecc_errors_total[5m])) by (device)` returns a jump on gpu-node-37:gpu1.

Jorge L: From runtime side, streaming stalls look like KV cache eviction + long kernel launches. Logs show repeated soft ECC errors and GPU reset attempts. Snippet:
```
[1800123332] nvidia: GPU 1 ECC corrected errors incremented: +42
[1800123340] nvml: thermal throttle start on GPU 1
[1800123352] driver: GPU reset succeeded
[1800123361] runtime: session stalled waiting for kernel completion (timeout)
```

Alex S: Impact: traffic to model-render-prod is seeing p95 from 120ms -> 2.1s. Customers on streaming endpoints experience stalls. Maya — any active customers escalating?

Maya C: CS queue has two inbound from a large customer experiencing partial stream truncation and increased latency; they're asking for ETA. I'll update them after mitigation plan.

Daniel K: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Drain affected GPU node gpu-node-37 from scheduling; 2) Route traffic off to healthy pool; 3) If capacity tight, turn on fallback to quantized-cpu variant for streaming endpoints for affected customers. Approving drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

infra-bot: Action queued: cordon gpu-node-37, starting drain. Estimated pod evict time ~30s-2m depending on active sessions.

Priya R: I'm also going to blacklist GPU device GPU1 on that node at the driver level so remaining pods don't pick it up: `nvidia-smi -i 1 -pm 0 && nvidia-smi -i 1 --gpu-reset` and add device blacklist to node config so kubelet reports reduced GPU capacity. Doing that now.

Jorge L: Routing config change: update smart-routing policy to prefer us-west-2b healthy subset and increase fallback weight to CPU-quantized by 30% for streaming routes. Patch pushed to routing service: `PATCH /routing/policies/streaming` with `fallback_ratio:0.3` — applying.

Alex S: Observability: enabling extended profiling for affected model to capture kernel timings and tail latencies (perf traces + nvprof capture for one pod). This is low-traffic capture, won't block.

incident-bot: gpu-node-37 cordoned and drain started at 1800123490. Migration started for 12 pods.

Daniel K: Drain finished for most pods, two long-lived streaming sessions still draining — we initiated graceful session handoff. Traffic to gpu-node-37 is at 0.

Priya R: Blacklist applied, nvidia-smi shows GPU1 in a disabled state. dmesg still shows occasional corrected ECC errors, but no more thermal throttle events after we adjusted node power profile. Posting recent lines:
```
[1800123420] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, ECC corrected error count 45
[1800123442] nvlddmkm: thermal event detected - throttling GPU 1
[1800123560] nvidia-smi: GPU1 disabled via admin-blacklist
[1800123600] kernel: driver reported GPU reset
```

Jorge L: After routing change, p95 dropped to ~160ms and p99 trending down to ~700ms within 2m. Streaming stalls reduced significantly.

Alex S: Marking incident as partially mitigated. We still have degraded nodes (gpu-node-39 showing intermittent ECC). We should schedule a maintenance drain for gpu-node-39 as well and consider a capacity bump in the Dedicated pool to avoid relying on CPU fallback long-term.

Maya C: I'll send a customer update: short note explaining transient GPU hardware issue, mitigation performed, we routed traffic and enabled fallback, monitoring for stability. ETA for full resolution TBD, will coordinate with infra.

Daniel K: Handoff: I'm going offline for a 10m break, Alex taking secondary on-call until I return. Alex, can you continue follow-up and vendor escalation?

Alex S: Affirmative. I'll escalate an SR with the hardware vendor with ECC logs and thermal traces. Opening ticket SR-1800 with vendor. Also scheduling a maintenance window to repro in a controlled environment.

Priya R: Action items recorded:
- escalate SR with vendor (Alex)
- schedule maintenance drain for gpu-node-39 (Priya)
- temporary capacity increase on Dedicated pool + rollback plan (Jorge)
- postmortem capture and add canonical runbook for thermal/ECC (Daniel/Alex)

Jorge L: For rollback/mitigation if more nodes hit: automated policy to increase fallback_ratio to 0.6 and enable static burst capacity from reserved pool. I'll work on a quick patch and a kill-switch.

infra-bot: Incident playbook updated: `incident/thermal-ecc` playbook linked.

Daniel K: Back from break, thanks Alex. Any remaining customer-impacting symptoms?

Alex S: No new escalations. p95 stable ~140-170ms across the cluster, p99 ~450-800ms depending on route. Keeping incident open for vendor fix and node replacement verification.

Maya C: Sent initial customer message to affected accounts. Will follow-up once vendor confirms hardware replacement schedule.

Priya R: Scheduling controlled repro and health check for all GPU nodes to detect ECC/thermal pre-failures. Running `nvmlDeviceGetXidErrors` sweep now. Expect results in ~20m.

Jorge L: Logging the temporary routing/fallback changes as a canaryable flag so we can quickly revert. Also recording cost impact estimate from CPU fallback (~+18% tokens cost temporarily).

Alex S: OK. I'll keep monitoring and will call for full incident postmortem once vendor confirms root cause. For now: Severity lowered to S2 (partial degradation, active mitigations).

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity S2. Thread will remain open until vendor SR closed and replacement validated.
